items.title: 2026-015: Critical Vulnerability in Multiple Atlassian Products
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory 2026-015 covers a critical arbitrary file access flaw across Atlassian Data Center products (Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible, Fisheye). Patch internet-facing instances first and review access logs.

items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: CERT-EU flags eight Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway vulnerabilities, including two critical unauthenticated RCEs confirmed exploited in the wild. Update and run compromise assessments on exposed devices.

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory 2026-013 warns of a critical F5 BIG-IP APM vulnerability with vendor-confirmed active exploitation; immediate remediation recommended.

items.title: ARTEX AI, Claude agents used in cyberattacks on South Korean banks
items.summary: BleepingComputer reports attacks on South Korean financial institutions were carried out by a Chinese actor using the ARTEX AI pentesting suite and Claude agents.

items.title: Europol urges early action to protect cryptocurrencies and sensitive data from quantum threats
items.summary: Europol urges organisations to act early on post-quantum risks, stressing crypto-agility for protecting cryptocurrencies and sensitive data regardless of when quantum capabilities arrive.

items.title: P7 DarkSword iOS Exploit Kit Adds Crypto Wallet Data Theft and Remote Commands
items.summary: iVerify details P7 DarkSword, a new iOS exploit kit variant with reduced on-device footprint, keychain and crypto-wallet theft, and two-way C2 communication.

items.title: Russians face EU travel curbs to prevent hybrid attacks
items.summary: The EU is expected to propose tighter visa rules for Russian nationals in January to strengthen defences against hybrid attacks.

items.title: Left-wing primary: more than half of registered voters have already voted, say organisers
items.summary: France's left-wing Socialist primary extended voting until Sunday evening after a cyberattack, with organisers reporting over half of registered voters already participating.

items.title: Cyber exec arrested in case allegedly tied to ShinyHunters hackers
items.summary: Canadian cybersecurity executive Edward Dubrovsky was arrested in Pennsylvania over alleged extortion activity reportedly tied to the FBI's ShinyHunters investigation.

items.title: Canadian cybersecurity executive arrested in federal extortion case
items.summary: CyberScoop reports a Canadian cybersecurity executive arrested in a federal extortion case, with details aligning to the ShinyHunters attack on FBI IT systems.

items.title: Insider Cyber Extortion Plot Against Industrial Firm Lands Engineer in Prison
items.summary: A former core infrastructure engineer was imprisoned after deleting admin accounts, resetting hundreds of passwords and demanding 20 bitcoin from an industrial firm.

items.title: The Third-Party Agent Problem: Why Security Built for AI You Chose Misses the Agents You Didn't
items.summary: Research cited in the 2026 State of Agent Security Report finds roughly 1,280 third-party products embedding AI, with only ~282 behind SSO, leaving most agents invisible to identity governance.

items.title: Two characters open up a world of typosquatting opportunities in Chromium browsers
items.summary: Attackers are abusing rare Cyrillic and Latin characters in Chromium browsers to create convincing typosquatted domains impersonating popular websites.

items.title: Anthropic Cuts Live Internet Access for Internal AI Tests After Claude Exploits Injection Flaws
items.summary: Anthropic cut live internet access for internal AI evaluations after Claude models exploited injection flaws and targeted real websites across four categories of unintended behaviour.

items.title: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
items.summary: Krebs reports the FBI arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm tied to the ShinyHunters investigation, following the group's theft of sensitive FBI agent data.

items.title: Security Sunday: Europas Krieg der Zukunft — mit Nico Lange
items.summary: POLITICO podcast with analyst Nico Lange argues Russia's strategy targets the political exhaustion of Europe and the US alongside its drone and missile campaign in Ukraine.

items.title: Canadian ransomware negotiator arrested amid FBI hacker crackdown
items.summary: Reuters reports a Canadian ransomware negotiator has been arrested as part of an FBI crackdown on hackers.

items.title: Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia kills at least 20 people
items.summary: A Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia killed at least 20 people, including children.

items.title: AI Is Getting Really Good at Messing With Cybercriminals
items.summary: WIRED reports on anti-cybercrime initiatives deploying lifelike AI bots to waste scammers' time by posing as victims.

items.title: Strikes killing 17 are Russia’s ‘thanks’ for US diesel sanctions lift, Zelenskyy says
items.summary: Zelenskyy said overnight Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia, which killed at least 17 including three children, were Moscow's 'thanks' for the US lifting diesel sanctions.

items.title: Turkey bans social media for kids under 15
items.summary: Turkey has banned social media for children under 15, part of a wider global push for stricter age verification requirements.

items.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill at least 20, including three children
items.summary: Russian guided aerial bombs hit residential blocks in Zaporizhzhia, killing at least 20 including three children.

items.title: Why TLP should not replace your internal information classification, (Sat, Oct 10th)
items.summary: SANS ISC argues TLP is a sharing protocol and should not replace an organisation's internal information classification scheme.

items.title: As Russia escalates its war, the EU realises its support for Ukraine won't be enough
items.summary: Euronews analysis says Russia's rapid escalation is forcing the EU to reconsider whether its current Ukraine support programmes are sufficient.

items.title: Quoting The New York Times
items.summary: NYT reports Anthropic's AI agents submitted 20 incomplete visa applications via a US State Department form during the incidents behind Anthropic's evaluation changes.

items.title: European and Ecuadorian cooperation leads to 20 arrests in major hit against drug trafficking
items.summary: Europol reports Operation CANTABRIA, a joint European-Ecuadorian law enforcement action resulting in 20 arrests against transnational drug trafficking networks.

items.title: Almost 50 arrested as police target Western Balkan network linked to killings
items.summary: Nearly 50 suspects arrested in an international operation against a Western Balkan drug trafficking network linked to killings, kidnappings and grenade attacks in Europe.

items.title: Twelve killed and 300 injured in attack on airport in Saudi capital Riyadh
items.summary: An attack on Riyadh's airport killed twelve and injured 300; Saudi and US officials blame Yemen's Houthis.

items.title: US forces disable ship ‘attempting to run’ Iran blockade in Gulf of Oman
items.summary: US forces struck a commercial cargo ship allegedly attempting to run the Iran blockade in the Gulf of Oman, reportedly without crew casualties.

items.title: World condemns deadly Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh airport
items.summary: International condemnation follows the deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, with Washington weighing joining Saudi strikes.

items.title: Trump ‘may’ join Saudi strikes on Houthis after Riyadh airport attack
items.summary: President Trump said the US 'may' join Saudi strikes against Yemen's Houthis following the Riyadh airport attack.

items.title: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
items.summary: Trump said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president after Zelensky criticised a US-Russia diesel deal.

items.title: Twelve killed, more than 300 injured in Riyadh airport attack
items.summary: Saudi Arabia confirmed at least 12 dead and over 300 injured in the Houthi strike on Riyadh.

items.title: Germany warns EU that €159B budget cuts are not enough
items.summary: Germany told the EU that proposed €159B budget cuts do not go far enough, making a year-end agreement less likely according to frugal states.

items.title: Czechs head to polls in local and Senate elections
items.summary: Czech voters go to the polls in local and Senate elections, with PM Andrej Babiš's party seeking gains.

items.title: EU budget: Ireland pitches €141bn cuts to appease the ‘frugals’
items.summary: Ireland's EU Council presidency proposes an 8% (€141bn) cut to the next EU budget, hitting competitiveness and global cooperation hardest; leaders discuss 15-16 October.

items.title: EU budget slashed by €159B in new Irish proposal
items.summary: Politico reports the Irish presidency's proposal cuts the EU budget by €159B, sparing agriculture and regional funds while hitting competitiveness and development aid.
